model_selection_rationale: HistGradientBoosting was selected as the non-linear implementation candidate. In 5-fold cross-validation on training data, Random Forest (ROC-AUC: 0.8137 +/- 0.0082), Logistic Regression (0.8122 +/- 0.0084), and Gradient Boosting (0.8110 +/- 0.0059) demonstrated comparable discrimination within one fold standard deviation. On the held-out test set, Logistic Regression achieved higher test ROC-AUC (0.8349 vs 0.8205). Gradient Boosting is preserved as the non-linear tree implementation candidate without asserting that it is objectively the best model.
feature_composition_summary: Non-laboratory predictor battery comprising demographics (5), anthropometrics (4), vitals and hemodynamics (5), lifestyle habits (5), and selected medical history variables (diagnosed diabetes, general health score, PHQ-9 depression score, coronary heart disease history, and stroke history).
threshold_selection_methodology: Derived strictly from training-set 5-fold cross-validation out-of-fold predictions targeting sensitivity >= 80% with specificity >= 20%. The held-out test set was completely quarantined during threshold selection.
survey_weighting_note: Survey-weighted metrics represent weighted test-sample estimates using NHANES MEC examination weights (survey_weight_mec_2yr / WTMEC2YR) adjusting for unequal selection probabilities and examination non-response. Weighting alone does not establish prospective clinical validity or external population generalizability.
